newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rescue teams free people trapped in Russian tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Rescue teams free people trapped in Russian tunnel.

text.p: Rescue teams using helicopters on Wednesday evacuated dozens of people trapped for almost a week by avalanches in a tunnel in the Caucasus mountains, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass, which had previously put the number of stranded people at about 300, quoted a government official in the North Ossetia region of southern Russia as saying all passengers had now been flown to safety in the nearby city of Vladikavkaz.
Some drivers had chosen to remain with their trapped vehicles, it said. Rescue workers had taken them food, warm clothing and medicines and were in constant radio contact.

"All the passengers of the vehicles which were snowbound for several days near Roksky Tunnel on the Transcaucasus highway were evacuated today to Vladikavkaz," Nikolai Makoyev, head of the North Ossetian Emergencies Ministry, said.
"They have been given the necessary assistance and fortunately there are no injured or sick people."

The minister said the situation was still difficult because of continuing avalanches and landslides near the four-km (2.5 mile) tunnel, which links North Ossetia and the breakaway Georgian province of South Ossetia.
Russian news agencies said earlier this week that some motorists had refused to leave their vehicles during earlier rescue attempts in case their cars were stolen or looted.
Tass said on Monday that two women had given birth while trapped in the tunnel and one new-born child had died of the cold. Two other people were reported to have died in the area at the weekend.
